Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Synthera evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production LLM inference. Key topics: reserved GPU sizing, burst hot-pool strategy, tenant isolation / fencing, VPC & KMS requirements, fallback to hosted variants, cost vs latency tradeoffs. Action items: pricing deck, perf benchmark, traffic profile.

Topics: reserved capacity sizing; isolation (multi-tenant vs dedicated nodes); burst handling and prewarm; private/VPC and KMS; success criteria and timeline; perf test plan.

Action items (captured in metadata above): see list.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intro from us — I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with Synthera, and Ravi is our SE. we wanted to run through your infra constraints and make sure reserved nodes would actually fit your workload.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: Hey Maya, thanks. I'm Lena, I run platform. Jamal is here from SRE and Priya is our ML lead. We're trying to understand whether reserved GPUs make sense versus staying on hosted during spikes. also curious about VPC and encryption story.
[00:36] Jamal Reeves: yeah, timeline—Q3 pilot, production by Q4 if numbers look sane. main worry: noisy neighbors, and how prewarm works when we have sudden bursts.
[00:50] Ravi Patel: cool. quick high level — Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved pools (hot or warm), you can configure isolation per-tenant or per-service, and we have policies for burst: warm-pool prewarm, emergency burst to shared capacity, and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants.
[01:12] Dr. Priya Anand: when you say "quantized variants" — are you talking 8-bit quantization? what's the perf delta for our 13B conversational model compared to full fp16?
[01:28] Ravi Patel: good question. typical 8-bit runs are 1.5x to 2x faster per-token, and cost is about 40–60% lower depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. but there's a quality delta; we can run evals on your prompt set so you can see.
[01:48] Lena Ortiz: re: isolation, we need guaranteed tenancy for PHI workload. can we have dedicated physical nodes for our org, and how does that affect SLOs and billing?
[02:02] Maya Chen: yes — Dedicated offers tenant-fenced node groups. it's a reserved node pool that you own logically, single-tenant. pricing is a reservation price + per-hour usage for burst, we can show both monthly and annual commit options.
[02:18] Jamal Reeves: any constraints on model size? we run a mix—some smaller 7B models for assistants and a 70B for research. we don't want the 70B stealing memory from the 7B workloads.
[02:32] Ravi Patel: you can pin model families to node pools; we recommend separating heavy models onto larger GPU types. for 70B you want A100/Pods-class or equivalent; 7B can sit on more cost-effective nodes. our placement engine prevents oversubscription of GPU memory across pinned pools.
[02:52] [crosstalk]
[03:00] Lena Ortiz: what's the failover if we lose dedicated nodes — do requests get dropped or bounced to hosted?
[03:06] Ravi Patel: primary fallback is to compatible hosted variants in the same region, subject to your fallback policy. you can set automatic fallback for non-critical routes, and preserve critical routes to stay queued or degrade to cached responses.
[03:20] Maya Chen: worth noting we have SLA tiers — reserved capacity SLAs cover uptime for the pool; fallback is an operational policy that you set. we'll include sample policies in the deck.
[03:36] Jamal Reeves: security — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO/SAML for tenancy-level RBAC. any gotchas?
[03:45] Ravi Patel: we integrate with customer KMS; on Private deployments you can bring your HSM. audit logs are available per request, and SAML/SCIM for SSO. minor quirk: some third-party KMS rotations require a short rolling restart of control-plane components on Private. we'll document that.
[04:10] Dr. Priya Anand: little bit more on perf: what's typical p99 latency for interactive chat at batch size 1 for a 13B? we're aiming for p95 sub-250ms.
[04:22] Ravi Patel: p99 will depend heavily on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. sterile numbers: for a 13B with short sequences (~50 tokens) on a V100-class unit you might see p95 around 180–220ms; on A10/A100 lower. again we should run your workload to verify — that's why the perf test is helpful.
[04:46] Lena Ortiz: about burst — we have very spiky load (campaign-driven bursts). how does hot-pool sizing work — do we prewarm n GPUs for x minutes? what's the billing for that?
[04:58] Maya Chen: we offer prewarm windows; you pay reservation for the hot pool plus a small per-minute prewarm fee if you exceed guaranteed throughput. the deck will have a burst calculator; we can plug your traffic to show expected costs.
[05:18] Jamal Reeves: On the prewarm — does prewarm keep KV caches warmed for prompt prefixes? our assistant uses long conversation contexts.
[05:26] Ravi Patel: prewarm can include prefix/KV caching for pinned sessions. but long-lived KV cache persistence increases memory needs; you can configure eviction policies. we'll recommend session-affinity and a sticky cache key pattern for long threads.
[05:46] [00:06 misunderstanding] Speaker 1: sorry, i said stick-y —
[05:52] Dr. Priya Anand: Another ask — we need to know how model rollouts work with reserved pools. e.g., can we rollback to a previous model if a new version regresses?
[06:05] Ravi Patel: yes — rollouts are supported. you can do canaries, percentage rollouts, and automatic rollback based on quality alerts. Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompt sets so you can detect regressions quickly.
[06:22] Lena Ortiz: what about on-prem path? we might need an air-gapped lab for certain datasets. is Private on-prem a different contract?
[06:31] Maya Chen: Private on-prem is a separate engagement — includes control-plane license, on-prem runtime, and support. we'd engage our solutions engineering + deployment team for that. it's typically longer lead time.
[06:46] Jamal Reeves: our SREs also care about maintenance windows. if you patch runtime, how disruptive is it?
[06:53] Ravi Patel: we support rolling upgrades for runtime; shard-level draining minimizes disruption. for control-plane upgrades we coordinate maintenance windows; for Dedicated customers we have an ops playbook that limits impact.
[07:07] Maya Chen: can we capture two quick numbers from you for sizing? peak concurrent requests per second during bursts, and typical request size (tokens in/out).
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: yes, we have a big campaign pattern that's ~2000 rps peak — though it's very short-lived — and baseline is around 120 rps. tokens per request about 80 on average, but some go up to 400.
[07:33] Jamal Reeves: also note we have strict data residency for EU customers; some traffic will need EU-only routing.
[07:40] Ravi Patel: we can route by region and you can pin EU traffic to EU node pools; also logging compliance for EU is doable with regional storage.
[07:54] Dr. Priya Anand: curious about cost model: reserved monthly vs annual — what's typical break-even?
[08:02] Maya Chen: break-even depends on utilization. if you hit 50–60% utilization of reserved capacity, monthly may be fine; annual commits usually get the best unit economics. we'll include a calculator with your traffic numbers.
[08:16] Lena Ortiz: competitor question — we evaluated SageMaker and another vendor — what's Redwood's angle?
[08:23] Maya Chen: Redwood focuses on inference economics and predictable SLOs across hosted/dedicated/private. less ops than self-hosting and more control than public hosted-only offerings.
[08:36] Jamal Reeves: any limits on autoscaling? we need predictable bursts but also cost caps.
[08:42] Ravi Patel: autoscaling is policy driven; you can set burst caps per-tenant and per-route and we support hard caps to prevent runaway costs. plus notifications to SREs.
[08:58] [pause]
[09:05] Maya Chen: ok let's talk about the perf test plan — Ravi, do you want to outline?
[09:09] Ravi Patel: sure — plan is: provision a dedicated pool with two node sizes (one for 13B, one for 7B), run 1-hour synthetic traffic replay using Synthera traces, measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll run both quantized and full precision variants.
[09:31] Lena Ortiz: we'll share anonymized traces. what do you need format-wise?
[09:36] Ravi Patel: a CSV with timestamp, request id, prompt token count, response token count, route id. if you have a replay harness we can ingest that too.
[09:46] Jamal Reeves: is the perf test billed?
[09:50] Maya Chen: initial perf test is complimentary as part of evaluation; extended benching beyond 4 hours might be billable. we'll note that in the follow-up.
[09:59] Dr. Priya Anand: on the eviction story — if node memory is constrained what happens to long conversations with KV cache?
[10:07] Ravi Patel: eviction happens based on LRU or configured TTL; we surface metrics so you can tune it. also you can reserve additional memory headroom for critical routes.
[10:20] Lena Ortiz: can we get request-level audit logs forwarded to our SIEM?
[10:26] Ravi Patel: yes, logs can be streamed to your SIEM, with options for TTL and redaction for PHI fields. we'll include recommended redaction rules.
[10:39] Maya Chen: quick check — what are your success criteria for pilot?
[10:43] Lena Ortiz: 1) p95 < 250ms for priority routes, 2) no data leakage and KMS integration validated, 3) predictable cost under burst scenario, and 4) rollouts working with canary.
[10:58] Maya Chen: perfect — we'll align the perf test to those.
[11:02] Jamal Reeves: about fallback — does fallback preserve request headers and tracing? we use Jaeger and have expensive downstreams.
[11:10] Ravi Patel: trace headers are preserved when routed; we maintain spans and tags so your APM should stitch. there is a small latency added during routing.
[11:20] [11:20 laughter] Speaker 2: okay great
[11:24] Dr. Priya Anand: any gotchas for model caching across restarts? we had issues in another system where cache warmed but then lost after a patch.
[11:33] Ravi Patel: we persist KV cache for session operators when configured; restarts of the worker will cause transient misses unless you have an external shared cache. we can advise on architecture.
[11:48] Lena Ortiz: last thing — procurement & contract: do you have a standard MSA for Dedicated?
[11:54] Maya Chen: yes we have an enterprise MSA and SOW for Dedicated/Private. we'll share a redline-friendly copy. typical procurement lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on legal.
[12:07] Jamal Reeves: security review — we may need SOC2 Type II and penetration test reports.
[12:13] Maya Chen: we can share SOC2 and compliance artifacts; for Private/On-prem we offer additional attestation.
[12:22] Dr. Priya Anand: ok that's helpful.
[12:26] Maya Chen: wrapping up — recap / next steps: I'll send pricing deck and burst calculator, Ravi will run perf test once you supply traces, and we'll set the SRE deep-dive for next week (proposed 2026-03-30).
[12:41] Lena Ortiz: yep, that works. thanks.
[12:44] Jamal Reeves: thanks, talk soon.
[12:46] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. bye.
